key_concepts: Burning wood is a chemical change called combustion
Heat from fire breaks down wood and releases energy as heat and light
Coal is a fossil fuel that releases carbon dioxide and other gases when burned
Solar and wind power are alternative energy sources
Heating coal, natural gas, and fuel oil changes them into other products
New Year celebrations involve temperature changes in fireworks and cooked foods
Burning garbage releases harmful pollutants into air, soil, and water
Pollutants from burning waste can harm plants, animals, and people
Recycling conserves natural resources, reduces pollution, and protects wildlife habitats
Improper waste disposal contaminates soil and pollutes air
